title: Memory Harnesses for Long-Running Research Agents — Stefania Druga, Sakana.ai
talk_summary: Sakana.ai's Stefania Druga frames memory as a harness-level write/manage/read control loop and tests recall policies on long-horizon tasks. She finds ranked decision-ledger recall beats vector RAG and memory gating when context overflows, while memory adds only cost when the task already fits in context.

takeaways.what_they_do: They give small agents zero durable memory and put memory in the harness as a write/manage/read loop, with core traces always shown and archival state across sessions.
takeaways.evidence_quote: you can think of memory as a write manage read loop

takeaways.what_they_do: They compare no memory, vector RAG, a ranked decisions ledger, and an oracle; the ranked ledger performed best for long-horizon recall.
takeaways.evidence_quote: the rank only ledger performed the best
takeaways.numbers: 68 questions; multiple cells and seeds; ranked ledger best on Xbench and Spider V2

takeaways.what_they_do: They test a no-memory baseline and find that when all task material fits in context, memory does not improve performance but does add cost.
takeaways.evidence_quote: It was the same performance with memory and without memory and it only added more cost.

takeaways.technique: Recall-policy eval with oracle and ablations
takeaways.what_they_do: They treat recall policy as a first-class metric and test recall modes against oracle ground truth plus wrong-step, recent-step, and arbitrary-example ablations.
takeaways.evidence_quote: consider the recall policy as a first class metric
takeaways.numbers: 68 questions; ablations with arbitrary, wrong, and most-recent steps

takeaways.technique: Penalize bad memory by cost and defects
takeaways.what_they_do: They argue bad memory is expensive because it burns tokens and can steer the agent wrong, while good structural recall saves budget.
takeaways.evidence_quote: bad memory is expensive because it spends more token and it can send agent the wrong way

takeaways.technique: Core trace plus archival across sessions
takeaways.what_they_do: Their harness always shows a core trace block and keeps an archival block for information across different sessions.
takeaways.evidence_quote: an archival block where I'm keep keeping track of information across different um sessions
